ashley (Support): Heads up — AcmeHealth (org_98765) opened saying ~12k credits gone overnight. They run a nightly ingest that calls batch embeddings at 02:00 UTC. Spike starts ~02:10 UTC.

josh (SRE): Can you paste the last worker logs around 02:10? Any 5xx or requeue storms?

ashley (Support): Pasting sanitized logs:

```
02:09:58 INFO enqueue job=ingest_batch id=job_0xabc size=500
02:10:03 ERROR worker-3 POST /v1/embeddings batch failed status=500 id=job_0xabc retrying
02:10:03 INFO enqueue retry job=ingest_single id=task_0x1 item=0
02:10:04 INFO enqueue retry job=ingest_single id=task_0x2 item=1
02:10:05 ERROR worker-1 POST /v1/embeddings single failed status=500 retrying
02:10:06 WARN lock expired key=cron-lock:nightly-ingest
02:10:07 INFO cron re-enqueue job=ingest_batch id=job_0xdef
02:10:08 INFO enqueue job=ingest_single id=task_0x3 item=0 (duplicate)
```

We see both batch failures and per-item requeues, plus the cron lock expired and the cron re-enqueued concurrently.

liam (ML Eng): If their client/backoff behavior falls back to per-item retries on batch failure, that can multiply calls. Which SDK/version?

ashley (Support): python-sdk 0.12.1 with auto_fallback=True in their config. Snippet from their client:

```
EmbeddingsClient(batch_mode=True, auto_fallback=True, timeout=30)
```

When batch fails the SDK issues single-item requests with retries for each item.

josh (SRE): That + cron re-enqueue + expired lock explains N * M calls (N = number of re-enqueued batches, M = items per batch). Probable root: flaky lock handling in their scheduler (k8s CronJob + a Redis-based lock with short TTL). New runner doesn't detect in-flight work and re-enqueues.

ashley (Support): Customer reports their billing UI shows many small embed calls (not batch) consuming credits. They want a refund; they're on a free trial.

kevin (Billing): We can do a manual credit adjustment for trial accounts. Need exact window + credit delta. Also want to verify no abuse. Please confirm: time window 02:08–02:18 UTC and affected org_98765.

ashley (Support): Confirmed. Approx breakdown: expected ~500 tokens/day; actual charged ~12,100 tokens overnight. I captured job ids. I'll open CS ticket.

deploy-bot: Deploy 2026.02.14-96 completed — no global infra incidents recorded in that window.

liam (ML Eng): Quick mitigation suggestions:
- Add idempotency header for enqueue operations (X-Redwood-Job-Id) so duplicate batches dedupe server-side.
- Change SDK fallback semantics: if batch fails with 5xx, do exponential backoff and requeue batch rather than per-item fallback.
- Increase lock TTL during batch enqueue/processing.

josh (SRE): Immediate operational steps:
- Disabled nightly cron for org_98765 at 04:30 UTC (stopped further burns).
- We should add a temporary server-side protection to reject rapid duplicate batch requests from the same job id for 10m.

kevin (Billing): I'll provision a 5k credit reversal now and mark for additional review pending final delta. Ticket CS-4321 created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/CS-4321

ashley (Support): Notified customer about temporary credit grant and that we're investigating. They acknowledged and paused their pipeline.

liam (ML Eng): I'll patch SDK behavior in 0.12.x branch (no per-item fallback on 5xx; prefer batch retry) and add an optional idempotency header helper. ETA EOD tomorrow.

josh (SRE): I'll implement server-side quick dedupe for job ids + extend lock TTL for cron-handler. Assign to me and infra team. ETA 48h.

kevin (Billing): Refund applied: 5000 promo credits (promo_2026_support) to org_98765. Will finalize additional credits after we confirm final counts.

ashley (Support): Closing loop for now — cron disabled, promo applied, customer notified. Will update CS-4321 with final numbers when infra has logs aggregated.

josh (SRE): Follow-up: found Redis lock TTL set to 5s in their helm chart. Recommending 5m for batch workflows. Noted in infra-templates.

ashley (Support): Thanks all. Will monitor and reopen if any more charge spikes. :white_check_mark:
